regress:cmp-02.note: Bodies are identical: they cover hashing/energy, 51% hash power, probabilistic finality, stake-based selection, slashing and low energy, but they expand PoS as 'Proof-of-Step', give only '51% of stake' with no 2/3 BFT threshold, and leave out nothing-at-stake, long-range attacks and weak subjectivity. The source lines differ but are of equal value (A: security budget; B: Peercoin 2012, which is correct).

regress:cry-002.note: A covers the practical trade-off (lattice-based, faster with smaller signatures, vs. hash-based, slower with larger signatures) but wrongly says SLH-DSA has larger public keys (they are tiny) and that its parameter sets mainly target categories 3 and 5 (1, 3 and 5 exist). B never states the size/speed difference and pads with obscure trivia, including a garbled 'security parameter n >= 221'.

regress:cry-009.note: Identical answers that cover trusted setup vs. transparency, proof size and hash vs. pairing assumptions (post-quantum). Both wrongly say SNARK verification scales linearly with the witness, call quasilinear 'sub-linear', and claim STARKs verify faster than SNARKs.

regress:cry-012.note: Identical: they correctly give cross-chain replay protection via the chain ID in the signature, but there is no v = chainId*2 + 35/36 formula and no ETH/ETC context. Both say Spurious Dragon activated in October 2016; it activated on 22 November 2016.

regress:cry-019.note: Identical: they correctly cover SP 800-208 (Oct 2020), OTS keys in a Merkle tree, why key reuse breaks security, and quantum resistance. Small inaccuracies (single-tree XMSS described as hierarchical, a 'public state') and the answer is cut off mid-LMS.

regress:num-02.note: Identical bodies with correct reasoning (499 s, about 8 min 20 s; 4.5e9 km, 15,000 s). However, the lead's '4 h 7 min' does not match the worked 4 h 10 min, and the text is cut off mid-formula. The source sections are equivalent.

regress:poi-04.note: Identical bodies name real hospitals (Pablo Tobon Uribe, San Vicente, Las Americas) but invent details: Clinica del Norte placed 'in El Poblado', and Pablo Tobon Uribe called a public E.S.E. hospital tied to the University of Antioquia that is less foreigner-friendly (it is a private non-profit). A's source check honestly says the sources are irrelevant; B lists irrelevant source facts (Bogota hospital 1564, a football club), which is padding.

regress:reason-04.note: Both compute 120 km/h and get 6 hours. A's source lines are relevant speed definitions; B's list unrelated Indian train timetables, which is irrelevant padding.

regress:tail-02.note: Identical bodies get the stigma right (Confucianism, criminal punishment) but invent the three styles ('Xiangyang (mountain river)', 'Jianghu', modern) and a fake proverb. The source sections then give the correct brush/realistic/splash-ink categories, so each answer contradicts itself. B also adds a line casting doubt on Confucianism as a cause.

regress:tail-12.note: Both correctly give the 1914 anthem, Andriy Khlyvnyuk of BoomBox, support for Ukraine and proceeds to the Ukraine Humanitarian Relief Fund. Neither gives the 8 April 2022 date or names Gilmour, so they are effectively equal.

regress:tech-10.note: Identical bodies give C/A/P definitions and the CP vs. AP choice under partition (using the usual 'two of three' simplification). Brewer is credited in both source sections; A adds the 1998/2000 history and the Gilbert-Lynch 2002 proof, B adds the CAP vs. ACID consistency distinction, both correct.

regress:trav-10.note: Both recommend T-money for subway and buses with transfers. A is more practical: fares, the 500-won deposit on single tickets, 30-minute transfers and the M-Pass. B says the Seoul subway 'consists of eight lines' (outdated and wrong today), describes the Mpass in a garbled way, and covers transfers only vaguely.

regress:trv2-08.note: Both cover ferries (Smyril, Teistin), village buses, helicopters, walking, Gasadalur, Leitisvatn and Torshavn's Tinganes, but leave out Mykines, Saksun, Gjogv, Vestmanna, Slaettaratindur and Mulafossur by name. B also mentions the tunnel/bridge road network and reads more coherently. A has a useful free red-bus detail but also advice to 'drive through Sorvagur', which contradicts the no-car question.

leadgate:lead-02.note: A names EMATE and estradiol sulfamate (E2MATE) but gives only breast cancer and leaves out Irosustat. B names Irosustat with breast, prostate and endometrial cancer, but wrongly hedges that it may not be Potter's work, and leaves out E2MATE. Neither mentions Reed, HRT/endometriosis or lung cancer.

leadgate:lead-04.note: Identical bodies are invented: the name from 'beatus'/Blessed Sacrament, a Church of Sao Domingos founded by 'Queen Santa Amelia', 'Homens Bons', a 'Marquis of Tombos', a royal palace in Alfama, and a claim that Beato played no role in 1640. A's source section gives the correct Beato Antonio (d. 1602) convent origin and Xabregas-Beato as an active centre of the conspiracy, contradicting its own body; B has no correction.

leadgate:lead-05.note: Both correctly give SR 65 north of SR 110 from 1923, SR 109 signed in 1930, full paving by 1939 and no changes since. B says which part was paved in 1930 (north of SR 110); A says only 'a section'. Neither mentions the reroute near Delta.

leadgate:lead-20.note: Identical near-refusals: both say the sources do not describe it and mention tree-felling and artillery only as hedged general knowledge. There is nothing on Featherston, Ferguson, Murphy's sailors or Rolling Fork.

leadgate:lead-21.note: Both are accurate. A has the 1960s gastarbeiter detail but no birth year and only part of the mother's jobs. B has 1978, the father's interpreter-and-translator work and all of the mother's jobs, but says only that the parents emigrated from West Anatolia.

leadgate:lead-28.note: Identical bodies invent the coaches: 'Teri Vanderslager' since 1984, 'Ralph Miller', and Jack Bauerle (a Georgia coach). A's source section correctly gives Jim Richardson, Mike Bottom (2012) and Matt Bowe, contradicting its body; B's source section gives only Matt Bowe.

leadgate:lead-29.note: A gives the D-gun-specific hazards (about 4000 C, acetylene explosion and burns, nobody in the room, a room built to withstand malfunction, gloves) but leaves out silicosis, siderosis and metal fume fever, and repeats itself. B gives only generic thermal-spray hazards (nanoparticle dust, noise, extraction, respirators) and none of the D-gun specifics.

leadgate:lead-31.note: Both give Cullen, Hermoso, Ramirez and 1974. A also covers the association of 720 mothers, the 1993 class action and the $650,000 USAID resolution, though not Cullen's Irish Columban background or Nobel nominations. B wrongly says the sources show no PREDA work for Amerasians.

regressgate:cry-009.note: Identical answers (same as regress:cry-009): they cover setup, transparency, proof size and hash vs. pairing assumptions, but wrongly say SNARK verification scales linearly and that STARKs verify faster.

regressgate:tech-10.note: Identical bodies, and the source sections carry the same facts (Brewer 1998/2000, Gilbert-Lynch 2002, the CAP availability definition), all correct.
